Starter guides from [Data Science Services](https://www.iq.harvard.edu/data-science-services) at the Institute for Quantitative Social Science, Harvard University, for the tools around research: version control, a website of your own, an editor, and writing in LaTeX. Each guide is a section in the sidebar and short enough to read in one sitting.

- [Git and GitHub](git/index.qmd): installing Git, a GitHub account, authentication, creating and cloning repositories, and the command line.
- [GitHub Pages](pages/index.qmd): a personal website, three ways: Google Sites, GitHub's online editor, or RStudio and Git.
- [VS Code](vscode/index.qmd): installing VS Code, with our recommended extensions, settings, and shortcuts.
- [Emacs](emacs/index.qmd): installing Emacs with our configuration, and the keys and commands you will use every day.
- [LaTeX](latex/index.qmd): the ways to write LaTeX (Overleaf, VS Code, Emacs) compared, and the documents you will write.
- [Overleaf](overleaf/index.qmd): signing up, editing, collaborating, and exporting.

The workshops (R, Python, Stata) are at [iqss.github.io/dss-workshops](https://iqss.github.io/dss-workshops/); everything DSS offers is listed under [Training materials](https://iqss.github.io/dss-training/).
